Commentary.Commentary: Back for the second innings! The umpires are back out in the middle, followed by the players of Sri Lanka Women. Also, out walk the two openers of South Africa Women, where the skipper, Laura Wolvaardt, will open the innings alongside Tazmin Brits.
... The Run Chase ...

Vishmi, back from injury, came out to bat, and she, along with Nilakshika Silva, added crucial runs, taking Sri Lanka past 100 before wickets tumbled again at the death. Okay, the DLS adjudged target is 121. A score of 105/7 might look modest, but with a DLS-adjusted target of 121, there’s still enough spice for South Africa to chew on. Can they chase calmly under lights? Or will Sri Lanka’s spinners script a twisty seque? The chase is in a bit.

South Africa's Nonkululeko Mlaba is up for a quick chat with Alan Wilkins. She tells that it was very tough to grip and bowl due to the seam being wet. Also shares that the outfield is very slippery and they focused more on collecting the ball cleanly. Also admits that it was a bit difficult to switch to the T20 mode and that she had to make some adjustments. Ends by saying that they are confident to chase this target down as the team is in a T20 mode now.

Vishmi Gunarathne looked sharp early on but took a nasty blow on her left knee that saw her stretchered off. Klaas then knocked over Hasini Perera and trapped Chamari LBW right at the end of the Powerplay. At 37/2, Sri Lanka were just wobbling. Then came the rain! The match stopped for around five long hours with Sri Lanka at 46/2, and when play finally resumed, it was a T20I masquerading as an ODI. Harshitha and Dilhari tried to resume and rebuild but were sent packing quickly by Mlaba and de Klerk. Mlaba ended with three key wickets, while Klaas and de Klerk were tight, tidy, and terrific with the ball. South Africa’s bowlers really showed how to adapt when conditions flipped like a coin.

Rain, drama, injuries, and wickets! We'd seen all. What started as a 50-over game turned into a sprint of 20 overs after a close to five-hour-long rain battle. Sri Lanka managed 105/7, but the target for South Africa has now been revised via DLS. Chamari Athapaththu won the toss and backed her instincts to bat first, but things didn’t go as smoothly as planned.

Commentary.Commentary: So, after a looooooong wait, of almost five hours, we are ready to resume. The umpires make their way out and the Proteas spread out of the huddle to take their positions. Harshitha Samarawickrama and Kavisha Dilhari stride out to resume their innings. Remember, it is a 20-over per side contest. And according to the revised playing conditions, the Powerplay for the second inning will be of 4 overs. Five bowlers can bowl a maximum of four overs, which means, Kapp and Klaas won't get to bowl as they already bowled five overs each. Nonkululeko Mlaba will bowl. Dilhari to face. Here we go...

UPDATE - 3.23 pm GMT - Right, so there is a discussion going on between both on-field umpires and both skippers around the strip. The official word on the starting time can come anytime now. Okay, so here is the official starting time - 3.40 pm GMT, and we would have a 20-over-per-side game, which means, the remaining 8 overs of the first inning would get completed, and then we would have a full 20-overs second innings. The target will be adjusted through DLS.

UPDATE - 3.14 pm GMT - Both the on-field umpires have stridden out for the inspection. The players from both teams are indulged in doing warm-ups and getting ready for the resumption while there is a chat going on between the head of the ground staff and the umpires. All the covers are peeled off now. There have been some muddy patches beside the boundary cushions created by the persistent rain, and the on-field umpires aren't happy with that, as the Super Soppers and the ground staff are working hard to dust them.

UPDATE - 3.02 pm GMT - Almost all the covers have been removed completely, and the rain has stopped. The supersoppers are working, and we can have an official word on the resumption soon. The groundstaff have done a commendable job so far, and the large blue sheets have been peeled off. As mentioned on-air, the umpires would inspect the pitch first once the ground staff is done with their mop-up work, and we are expecting a starting time before 3.41 pm GMT.

UPDATE - 2.46 pm GMT - Now, the umpires have moved towards the pitch, and they are inspecting it. Also, we would have an expected official update at 3 pm GMT, as mentioned on-air. Suddenly, the vibe has changed, and we can hope for a result out of this match, which looked highly unlikely at one point in time.

UPDATE - 2.41 pm GMT - Finally, we have some genuinely positive news! The steady rain appears to have eased significantly. The umpires have now walked out and are engaged in a discussion near the boundary cushions. Crucially, both team captains have joined them for a chat. This flurry of activity strongly suggests that we'll be hearing an official update on the potential start time and playing conditions very soon, as the ground staff are gradually removing the covers and have started to do their mop-up work. The hope for play is definitely back on. We still have exactly an hour remaining for the cut-off time.

So, what happens if this one ends up being a washout too? Both teams will share a point each, as has been the case here in Colombo, where the real challenge seems to be earning more than a single point! Jokes aside, South Africa will move up to 7 points, drawing level with England, but will remain third due to a lower net run rate. While Sri Lanka Women will climb a spot to sixth place with 3 points. But that would do very little to an already turbulent campaign.

UPDATE - 2.07 pm GMT - Nope, the rain hasn’t eased up one bit. It’s been a steady downpour since the interruption. Looking at the live visuals, it really doesn’t seem like we’ll get any cricket from here on. Apart from the DJ trying to keep the energy alive, there’s nothing much happening inside the stadium. Only a handful of hopeful spectators remain in the stands, but honestly, it doesn’t look promising. The tick-tock continues as we approach the cut-off time.

UPDATE - 1.16 pm GMT - We've reached the point where the cut-off time for a 20-over-per-side contest is 3.41 pm GMT, leaving us with over two hours of time to play with. As mentioned by Natalie Germanos on air, to complete the match, we need a total of 20 overs across both innings, meaning we need to get through the remaining eight overs of this innings and then a full 20-over second innings. The challenge, however, is the steady rain currently falling.

UPDATE - 12.49 pm GMT - The relentless downpour continues, and as time slips away, the chances of a resumption look increasingly bleak. Another washout in Colombo now appears to be on the cards, and we can only wait to see if the weather offers a window for the players to return to the field. Adding to the frustration, the ground staff remains helpless, as they cannot begin their work until the rain stops, and that looks unlikely anytime soon.

UPDATE - 12.14 pm GMT - Live visuals show nothing but blue sheets covering the entire playing area as the rain continues to lash down heavily. It’s been nearly two hours since play was interrupted. Sri Lanka Women have already endured two washouts, one against Australia and another against New Zealand, where they were in a commanding position and eyeing valuable points. You’ve got to feel for them, because if this game meets the same fate, their qualification hopes will take a serious hit with only a couple of games remaining on the roster. So far, they have played only one complete game, against England, while their opening fixture against India was shortened, where they faced a defeat with the DLS method coming into play.

UPDATE - 11.58 am GMT - There is still no change in the status, as the steady, persistent rain continues to fall and the entire playing area remains under the covers. With ominous forecasts suggesting the long wait is far from over, and with precious time now officially getting lost, the focus is on when play will resume and the result, as this match is crucial for both teams. For now, the rain is increasing the collective frustration for players and fans enduring this dreary, unmoving delay.

UPDATE - 11.33 am GMT - The long delay due to the weather has now officially resulted in overs being lost, meaning that whenever the action finally begins, this game will be shortened. While it's disappointing to lose time, the focus now shifts to waiting for the rain to stop so the ground staff can prepare the field for a quick restart, albeit a shortened one.

UPDATE - 11.24 am GMT - Since the rain is persistent, there is no new update on the situation, as the wait continues. Even if the rain stops now, play wouldn't resume right away, as the groundstaff and supersoppers would need a significant amount of time to clear the water from the field. For now, the frustration remains the same, the covers remain firmly, and we continue to wait for a break in the weather.

UPDATE - 10.57 am GMT - Alan Wilkins, on air, informs that overs will start being reduced after 30 minutes if the rain doesn’t relent. But for now, it continues to rain heavily in Colombo with menacing dark clouds overhead. Also, a positive bit of news from the Sri Lankan camp is that Vishmi Gunarathne will return to bat, with the latest reports confirming that she has no fracture. Currently, she is receiving the required medical treatment.

UPDATE - 10.43 am GMT - It continues to pour, heavier than before, in fact. For those wondering about the persistent spell of bad weather in this part of the world, the Colombo City Council and the Disaster Management Center (DMC) have declared a state of emergency in the Sri Lankan capital, with forecasts warning of heavy to very heavy rain and strong winds expected to last until 18th October.

UPDATE - 10.26 am GMT - Uh...oh! The drizzle that was looming around has gotten a bit heavier, and the dark clouds are there, threatening the match on one side, while things look a bit brighter on the other side. The umpires have decided to call the covers on, and the big blue sheets have been brought on to cover the entire ground. Hoping for the best, but for now, the players have walked off the field.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match rituals and it is now time for the action to begin in Colombo. It is overcast, and the floodlights are switched on as well. The Proteas spread out of the huddle and take their respective fielding positions. Chamari Athapaththu will be accompanied by Vishmi Gunarathne to open for Sri Lanka Women. And as usual, Marizanne Kapp will open the attack with the new ball for South Africa Women. A couple of slips in place. Vishmi to face. Here we go...

The flags of both nations unfurl in the middle as it is now time for the national anthems. Both sets of players are getting lined up, followed by the match officials. It will be Sri Lanka's first, followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

Tharindu Perera, the Assistant Coach of Sri Lanka Women, steps up for a quick chat before the start of play. He says that the plan stays simple - to put runs on the board if they bat first, giving the bowlers a solid total to defend later on. And if they bowl first, the target is to restrict the opposition under 220, setting the tone early in the match. Reflecting on their previous outing, he feels the opening partnership laid a great foundation, allowing the experienced players to build on that momentum. Praises Nilakshi de Silva’s explosive knock, calling it a match-defining innings that powered them to a strong total. Speaking about the team’s mindset, Perera highlights that the group carries a lot of positive energy. Notes that the players have worked hard on reducing dot balls and focusing on strike rotation, which he believes will ease the pressure in the middle overs and keep the scoreboard ticking consistently. Concludes by saying that this Sri Lankan side is well-balanced and dangerous. With power-hitters ready to explode in the final overs, he insists that they are fully prepared to challenge any team that stands in their way.

PITCH REPORT - Pommie Mbangwa is pitchside with his analysis. Says it is 30 degrees Celsius with 78 percent humidity. Shares that pitch number 9 will be used for the game. About the dimensions, he informs that the square boundaries are 60 meters and 61 meters, respectively, whereas it is 70 meters down the ground. Stacy Ann-King joins him and closely observes that it is pretty dry and hard. Details that it will be good for batting if the batters apply themselves. Shares that 38 wickets have been taken by the seamers at this venue and reckons that since South Africa Women are playing their first game in Colombo, their seamers will enjoy bowling here a lot.

The South African skipper, Laura Wolvaardt, steps up and says that they don’t mind chasing, especially with recent success while batting second. With a bit of rain around, she feels that it’s smarter to bat later and adjust to the conditions as the match progresses. Points out that the conditions look quite different at this time of the year, and it’s important for the team to get used to them early. Calling it a nice wicket to bat on, she emphasises that the bowlers need to assess the surface quickly and hit the right areas up front. Reflecting on the tournament so far, Wolvaardt admits that it hasn’t been their best outing as a top order, but she insists that they’re working hard to improve and build momentum moving forward.

The captain of Sri Lanka Women, Chamari Athapaththu, says that they had a good game against New Zealand, where they batted pretty well, but says it is unfortunate that it was abandoned due to rain. Says the weather is not under their control, but stresses on playing a good brand of cricket and sticking to the plans. Highlights that they have done well against South Africa, at home and away, and drawing inspiration from that, Chamari expects her side to do well overall. Informs that they are going with the same Playing XI.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Sune Luus (In place of Anneke Bosch), Annerie Dercksen, Marizanne Kapp, Karabo Meso (WK) (In place of Sinalo Jafta), Chloe Tryon, Nadine De Klerk, Nondumiso Shangase (In place of Tumi Sekhukhune), Masabata Klaas, and Nonkululeko Mlaba.

Sri Lanka Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Chamari Athapaththu (C), Vishmi Gunarathne, Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Piumi Wathsala, Sugandika Kumari, Malki Madara, and Inoka Ranaweera.

TOSS - Both skippers walk out for the toss, with the weather holding up for now, and the conditions are looking dry. Laura Wolvaardt flips the coin and Chamari Athapaththu calls 'Heads'. It lands 'Heads' and Sri Lanka Women win the toss. They have elected to BAT first.

Key battles? Oh, there are some spicy ones if we get action to see. Laura Wolvaardt vs Inoka Ranaweera, Chamari Athapaththu vs Ayabonga Khaka, and of course, the mid-over duel of Kapp vs Nilakshika Silva. It’s all set to be a mix of strategy, grit, and maybe a bit of rain-soaked chaos. Can the Proteas roll into the semis with swagger, or will the Lankan roar finally echo through Colombo? Strap in for more updates!

And speaking of the pitch - expect a typical R. Premadasa surface. Early on, it’ll play nice for the batters, but as the day drags on, those spinners will be licking their fingers. The surface gets slower, grip increases, and batting second can become very tough. That’s why the toss will be GOLD today, and also considering the fact that the rain is looming as well. Remember, Sri Lanka’s left-armers like Ranaweera and Sugandika Kumari can be tricky here, but Mlaba and others won’t back down either.

Okay, now, the big spoiler - the WEATHER! Colombo skies have turned moodier, and the forecasts indicate that rain chances will fluctuate throughout the day, which means we may experience interruptions, frustration, and possibly even a bit of DLS drama (yay?). The covers will be out faster if clouds roll in, and players might just have to stay mentally sharp for a stop-start affair. If there’s one thing both sides need today, it’s patience.

Meanwhile, Sri Lanka… oh dear, what do you do when the skies keep trolling you? Two washouts, one heartbreak, one hammering - this team has seen it all. Chamari Athapaththu, the lion-hearted skipper, keeps roaring, but the rest need to start echoing that roar. Nilakshika Silva has been their silver lining - that 28-ball 55 not out against New Zealand was fireworks in slow motion, but she needs support. Can Harshitha Samarawickrama and Dilhari finally chip in to give Sri Lanka a full batting performance? Because if they do, they can punch above their weight, especially in these sticky, spin-friendly home conditions.

South Africa walk in like that confident student who bombed the first test but aced every exam since. Three back-to-back wins after that setback start against England have completely changed their mood and mojo. Laura Wolvaardt is back in form, and she has 546 runs against Sri Lanka at an average of 91 in ODIs. Seriously, that’s alien-level consistency against the island nation, while de Klerk and Kapp have turned into crisis managers who just don’t panic, as we saw in the last couple of matches. But the Proteas would be eyeing a clinical win instead of another late chase thriller. They’d love that, and with Sune Luus back from injury, that middle order just got a power-up.
